chunks: And Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Musa ibn Umar from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, who said:
Safwan ibn Yahya asked Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj about Dhihar, and I was present. He said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'When a man says to his wife,

The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And the expiation is freeing a slave. If he cannot find [one], then fasting for two consecutive months. If he cannot manage fasting, then feeding sixty poor people. If he cannot find [the means for] feeding, it remains a debt upon him until he can pay it, and it is not permissible for him to have intercourse with his wife until he fulfills the obligation upon him.
ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for Dhihar in Shia jurisprudence if the man cannot free a slave?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that the binding nature of Dhihar is independent of consummation, a key distinction in Shia fiqh. It details the hierarchical expiation (kaffarah) of freeing a slave, fasting two months, or feeding sixty poor, noting that the husband remains prohibited from intimacy until the debt is cleared. This ruling underscores the seriousness of the oath as a form of temporary divorce requiring formal reconciliation.
